Armed / disarmed: the alarm system is sw: Armed / disarmed: the alarm system is switched on / off. There are three ways of being armed: Full protection – nobody is at home, doors, windows and motion detectors are watched. Perimeter protection – you are at home, only doors and windows are watched, you can move around freely inside. Night protection – like perimeter protection, but switched on by itself at night.
State: one single value in ioBroker, e.g: State: one single value in ioBroker, e.g. "kitchen window open" or "living room lamp on". You pick it with the button next to the field from the object list. Function: a group of states in ioBroker (Objects → Enumerations → Functions), e.g. "Windows" with all window contacts. If you have no such groups, simply put the devices into the tables "by hand".
The easiest way is a function (enum) of: The easiest way is a function (enum) of ioBroker – e.g. "Windows" with all window contacts. Everything in the function is monitored, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves. Press "Search automatically": Home Guard looks through your functions and fills in suitable ones – also lamps, presence and a door lock for the later steps. Only empty fields are filled; it takes about 15 seconds.
For sensors without a function, and for: For sensors without a function, and for the front door: add a row for the door you come in through and tick "delayed". Then opening it does not raise the alarm at once – you have the entry delay (next step) to switch the alarm system off. Tick "inverted" only if a sensor reports the wrong way round (shows "closed" when it is open). A row here overrides the same sensor from a function.

Leave "Value on/off" empty when it is simply switched on and off. "Runs on": an outside siren best only in full protection, so it does not wake the neighbours when you are at home.

Examples for the event "Alarm": outdoor lights or a socket on, roller shutters up, start a camera recording, the radio loud. With a second row and the event "Alarm ended" you switch it back. Other events, e.g. "Full protection armed": lock the door or roller shutters down. Value: true = on, false = off, a number for roller shutters or dimmers (e.g. 0 or 100). Scenes and scripts work too: the state of the scene, or for a script javascript.0.scriptEnabled.<name> with true.
